title: Kevin Porter Jr. Sets Sights on Bam Adebayo's Record While Invoking Kobe Bryant's Respect - NewsBreak
text:
By Shabiha Akter ,
1 hours ago
Kevin Porter Jr. (Image Credits: Imagn) The Milwaukee Bucks have endured a difficult season, and the franchise is reportedly planning to shut down Giannis Antetokounmpo for the remainder of the year . While the move may frustrate fans, it could create valuable opportunities for younger players on the roster to step into bigger roles and showcase their scoring ability. One player who appears especially eager for that chance is Kevin Porter Jr.
Porter Jr. has openly embraced the idea of taking on more offensive responsibility. During a recent livestream, Porter Jr. brought up Bam Adebayo’s massive 83-point performance and confidently stated that he believes he can surpass it someday, out of respect for Kobe Bryant.
“ 50 point game? I don’t know, I was out of my mind for real, for real. “I’m trying to drop 80. Shoutout to Kobe, shoutout to Bam, because I’m beating that one day. For sure. Now that Kobe got beat, I gotta beat Bam just for the respect of Kobe. You feel me ?” Porter Jr. said.
Adebayo’s 83-point outing stands as the highest individual scoring performance of the modern era. Adebayo achieved this by being fully empowered as the Miami Heat’s primary offensive option.
For Porter Jr. to realistically challenge that record, he would need a similar situation in Milwaukee. He needs an opportunity where the offense runs heavily through him, and the Bucks provide the green light to keep attacking throughout a game.
Kevin Porter Jr.’s Knee Issue Costs Him a Prime Chance to Go Big vs. Blazers On the court, Kevin Porter Jr. is currently dealing with right knee inflammation. It forced him to miss his fourth straight game on Wednesday against the Portland Trail Blazers. With Milwaukee already playing without Giannis Antetokounmpo, the game against a short-handed Blazers squad could have presented Porter Jr. with a perfect opportunity to chase Adebayo’s scoring mark.
Kevin Porter Jr. (image Credits: Imagn) There is still no definite timeline for his return, as the Bucks guard has appeared in only five games throughout March. In his second season with the Milwaukee Bucks, Porter Jr. has played 38 games and is averaging 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 7.4 assists per game
The 25-year-old arrived in Milwaukee at last season’s trade deadline. The Los Angeles Clippers dealt him to the Bucks in exchange for MarJon Beauchamp.
